clue.text: Bottle of Hollands?

parts.note: bottle is slang for nerve, and Hollands is Dutch gin, so this is the nerve that a drink of gin supplies

explanation.surface: A request for a bottle of Dutch gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a container, but in British slang it means courage; Hollands is a gin from the Netherlands, and the phrase means boldness found in drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names bravery that comes from alcohol, here punningly read as a bottle of gin from Holland.

clue.text: Diluting strain of French red wine going to Spain

parts.note: de is the French word for of
tent is a deep red Spanish wine
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A French red wine being watered down on its way to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' simply joins the pieces in order; TENT is an old name for a dark red wine from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A détente is an easing of tension between nations, so it waters down the strain.

clue.text: Royal 14 hill's farewell to Northerners

definitions.meaning: the hill in County Meath where the High Kings of Ireland were crowned; 14 is IRISH
... is a goodbye used in northern England

explanation.walkthrough: The 14 points to IRISH, the answer to 14-down. Ta-ra is an informal farewell heard in Lancashire and Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the spelling: the ancient royal seat of Irish kings, and a northern English way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Queen traps old native deer in Bantustan

indicators.note: the Queen's letters close round and trap the next piece

parts.note: HM stands for Her Majesty
the eland is a large antelope native to Africa

explanation.surface: A monarch catching an elderly African deer in a southern African territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Bantustans were the territories set aside under apartheid South Africa, which fits the African eland in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantustans were officially called homelands, the reserves created for black South Africans under apartheid.

clue.text: E.g. Strauss's key?

definitions.meaning: Andrew Strauss was an England opening batsman in cricket
a key is something that unlocks a door

explanation.walkthrough: Strauss here is not the composer but the former England cricket captain, who opened the batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who starts the innings and a device that unlocks are both called by the same word.

clue.text: Yuri Gagarin orbited over this port in 3 (then)

indicators.note: Gagarin's name circles the four letters, which lie across its two words

explanation.surface: The first cosmonaut circling above a harbour city of his country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orbited' says the name surrounds the letters: yuRI GAgarin. 3 is HOMELAND, and Latvia was part of the Soviet Union, Gagarin's homeland, at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the Baltic capital and seaport of Latvia, then a Soviet republic.

clue.text: Where entrance to Alhambra's guarded by stunted old man

indicators.note: the first letter is kept safe inside the shortened word for an old man
cut short, so the old man word loses its final letter

parts.note: grandad is an informal word for an elderly man

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An old man of reduced height standing guard at the gate of the Moorish palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunted' clips GRANDAD to GRANDA, and 'guarded by' places the A of 'Alhambra' within it; 'Where' defines the place by the clue itself, as the Alhambra is there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra palace stands in the Andalusian city, so the clue's question names its location.

clue.text: Identical group triumphs over India's closest siblings

indicators.note: in this reading the word for identical spreads over and round the India letter

parts.note: identical means the same
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a set is a group
wins means triumphs

explanation.surface: A matching team beats India in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a loose container signal here: the India letter sits within the word for identical, not above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjoined twins are physically joined, making them siblings as close as can be.

clue.text: In the meantime, what to do with someone who's 'ad it?

definitions.meaning: provisional, for the period in between

definitions.text: what to do with someone who's 'ad it
definitions.meaning: a dropped-aitch Cockney 'bury him', said of someone who has died

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits as INTER 'IM: bury him, in the same dropped-H speech as ''ad it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Provisional arrangements cover the meantime; and burying a dead man is interring him.

clue.text: Country at odd angle adjacent to north Germany

indicators.note: something odd is out of the ordinary, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: D is the vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A nation set at a strange angle beside northern Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation of the United Kingdom, here simply called a country.

clue.text: Patisserie item US lawyer (29) cooked with effort

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney in the US

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: 29-across begins SPANISH, the word used here
a try is an effort

explanation.surface: An American attorney baking a pastry from Spain with hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: '(29)' points to the first word of 29-across as the fodder that 'cooked' rearranges into NISHPAS; a DA is an American prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet yeast pastry from Denmark, sold in bakeries and cake shops.

clue.text: Taxman's wandering round front in Castletown, finding pets there

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the single letter taken from the town
letters that wander stray from their places

parts.note: the whole word is used, including the S

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tax collector strolls around a town on the Isle of Man and comes across some animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Castletown is on the Isle of Man, which is what 'there' refers to; 'wandering' scrambles TAXMANS round the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailless cats are a breed native to the Isle of Man, the island the town belongs to.

clue.text: Dumps Royal Horse Guards

definitions.meaning: being in the dumps is low spirits
the regiment's nickname, from its blue uniform

explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Horse Guards, a British cavalry regiment, were nicknamed after their blue coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Low spirits are called by the colour of melancholy, which also names a cavalry regiment.

clue.text: See 29
24 on hot whiskey

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: 24-across is IRIS
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A number placed on a hot drink of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit distilled in Ireland, spelt with an e, is known simply by the nationality.

clue.text: Cavalry costs worried 29 king besieged by guerrillas' flanks

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters are disturbed
the Spanish king is surrounded by the outer letters
a word's flanks are its first and last letters

parts.note: rey is Spanish (29-across) for king

explanation.surface: Worries about the cost of a cavalry unit, with a Spanish king besieged by guerrillas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges COSTS. REY is the Spanish word for king, and the first and last letters of 'guerrillas' surround it.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous British cavalry regiment, named for its grey horses.

clue.text: Feature of post-watershed programmes holding sway over listener

indicators.note: the word for sway keeps the listener inside it

parts.note: to swing is to sway
an ear is what listens

explanation.surface: Late-night television that influences the viewer.
explanation.walkthrough: The watershed is 9pm on British TV, after which adult content such as bad language is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad language is permitted on British television only after the 9pm cutoff.

clue.text: Ringleader of 11 in film 13s …

definitions.meaning: Danny is the leader of the eleven thieves in the heist film
13 is MAIN, an old word for the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: The film is Ocean's Eleven, whose gang leader gives the possessive; the main is the sea, so mains are seas.
explanation.definitionFit: The heist leader's surname with a possessive, and the great seas, which the main also means.

clue.text: SA golfer gets green light as supporter of 30, perhaps

indicators.note: the golfer takes in, or gets, the signal to proceed

parts.note: Gary Player is a South African golfer
a go is a green light or permission

explanation.surface: A South African golfer is cleared to play as a theatre fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 30 is OLIVIER, the National Theatre stage, so its supporter is a theatre fan; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular theatre visitor supports theatres such as the Olivier.

clue.text: … believer in the robbery he abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so these letters are dropped from the robbery

parts.note: a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: Continuing the film theme: a man of faith in the heist that he walked away from.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the heist film of 17-across; 'abandoned' leaves IST once the pronoun goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is someone who believes in a god.

clue.text: Internet pen pal possibly recruits 14 in Gulf state

indicators.note: the online friend takes in the Irish abbreviation, as an employer takes on staff

parts.note: an e-mate is an email friend
IR is the abbreviation for Irish, the answer to 14

explanation.surface: An online friend signs up an Irishman in the Persian Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: IR abbreviates IRISH (14) and sits in E-MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A country ruled by an emir, such as those in the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Caught shifty chap pocketing sale item "Emblem of the Proletariat"

indicators.note: the outer letters slip the next piece into their pocket

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: shifty suggests moving about, so the letters change places

parts.note: a lot is an item at an auction

explanation.surface: A cricketer caught a dodgy character pinching something at an auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifty' rearranges the man's word to give HCAP; the flat cap was the working man's headgear in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat cap worn by working men became a symbol of the working class.

clue.text: 14 and 26 run amok, seizing unknown fan of Alexander

indicators.note: the jumbled letters grab hold of the unknown
running amok is chaotic, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: IR abbreviates Irish, the answer to 14
26 is CATS
Z is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Irish cats go wild, seizing a mystery admirer of Alexander.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander here is any of the Russian tsars of that name, not Alexander the Great; 'run amok' scrambles the letters round Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the Russian emperors, such as Alexander, backs that rule.

clue.text: King with a seat in Edinburgh

definitions.meaning: ... Seat is the hill overlooking Edinburgh

explanation.walkthrough: Arthur's Seat is an extinct volcano and park in the middle of Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary British monarch, whose name a hill in the Scottish capital also bears.

clue.text: Murdoch's flag

definitions.meaning: the first name of the novelist Dame ... Murdoch
the yellow flag is a wild plant of that kind

explanation.walkthrough: The novelist, not Rupert, and flag is a plant name, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish-born novelist's first name, and a flowering plant called a flag.

clue.text: See 15
See 11
King is head of state offering light touch

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A monarch is the figurehead whose rule is gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle brush of the lips is a soft contact.

clue.text: Member in bar dance, footless

indicators.note: a word without its foot loses its last letter

parts.note: the limbo is a dance under a lowered bar

explanation.surface: A dancer at a bar has lost a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a member of the body.

clue.text: Morsel of succulent chopped ham in paninis cooked in Caribbean

indicators.note: a morsel is a small piece, here just the first letter
the chopped meat goes inside the bread rolls
cooked means prepared, so the combined letters are reworked
chopped means cut up, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A bite of juicy diced ham in toasted sandwiches, eaten in the West Indies.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'succulent' leads; 'chopped' and 'cooked' scramble HAM and PANINIS together into PANISHMAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean coast and sea controlled by Spain were known by this historical name.

clue.text: NT's 13 stage musical about Italy

indicators.note: the musical's title goes round the Italian abbreviation

parts.note: Oliver! is a famous stage musical
I is the vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: The National Theatre's big auditorium hosts a musical about Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is MAIN: the Olivier is the National Theatre's largest stage in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest auditorium at the National Theatre is named after the actor Laurence Olivier.

clue.text: Snack was terrible, awfully hot inside

indicators.note: the hot letter goes inside the jumbled words
awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Food that was dreadful and badly burnt within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' is fodder, not the anagram signal: 'awfully' rearranges WAS TERRIBLE round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese melted on toast is a light dish, a classic snack.
